Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE...

India would have taken the score early on. Renuka Singh and Pooja Vastrakar were taken to cleaners in the first six overs but the spinners, Yadav, Sharma and Patil were called up once again to rescue and take wickets. India dropped two crucial wickets but didn't allow the batters to make the most of the lifeline. Apart from Sharma, all of them ended with a wicket each. Yadav was pick of the bowlers with two wickets. Right then! A below-par score. India have a chance to sale the series. Can they do so or Bangladesh Women will fight back?

A brilliant bowling performance by Indian bowlers yet again. The scorecard looks similar to what we saw in the second game. The top order were yet again in the mix of runs, scoring bulk of it but after the foundation the laid, wickets fell in tandems and Bangladesh lost the momentum in the middle and find phase. Bangladesh Women were in a really good position but we feel the two run outs which could have been avoided of Murshida Khatun and Sobhana Mostary shifted the momentum.

OUT! RUN OUT! Full and wide of off. Akter dabs it to third man for a single. Bangladesh Women try to sneak in another one but the keeper whips the bails off. Just one. Bangladesh Women end with 117 for 8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. A strong breeze flowing across and a bit cloudy as well. Overcast conditions and the rain could play its part today as well. Let's hope we get a full game. The Bangladeshi openers are out in the middle. Renuka Singh to bowl first. Let's play...
Nigar Sultana says they would have bowled first as well due to the conditions. Adds they were happy with how they batted in the second match and hopes the batters give a good start in this match too.

Harmanpreet Kaur says they will bowl first. Adds it is a new pitch and hopes to chase the target. Informs they are playing the same team. Shares they need to bowl more tight in the first six overs and hopes to do well in this match.

TOSS - India Women have won the toss and will BOWL.

Hello and welcome to the third T20I between India Women and Bangladesh Women. India Women lead the series 2-0 thanks to a brilliant performance in the first match and with a little bit of help on second match. The previous match was hampered by rain but India Women were well ahead the DLS score before it started pelting down. Bangladesh Women, on both occasion played decent cricket but were not upto the mark to get over the line. Their bowlers have performed well but they dearly need the batters to step up if they were to keep the series alive. Can they do so? Let's find out.
...MATCH DAY...

It is now time for the third T20I between Bangladesh Women and India Women at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium. Unlike the previous series between these two sides on Bangladeshi soil, this series has been anything but competitive so far, with India taking a comfortable 2-0 lead. With this being a five-match series, Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. will be looking to seal the series with a couple of games to go, whereas Nigar Sultana's Bangladesh will look to keep the series alive. In the second T20I, despite getting what they wanted, which was to bat first, it was yet another dismal performance from the hosts. Murshida Khatun was the lone warrior whose 46-run knock helped Bangalesh limp to 119. In reply, India were rocked early, but Dayalan Hemalatha took the Bangladesh bowlers to the sword. Her breezy knock ensured that India were ahead on the DLS par score when the rain came and no more play was possible, resulting in India making it 2-0. More than the bowling, it has been the batting that has let Bangladesh down big time. Other than the performances by Nigar Sultana and Murshida Khatun, there has not been much to write home about Bangladesh's batting. As they aim to bounce back, Dilara Akter, Sobhana Mostary, and Fahima Khatun must contribute effectively with the bat. On the bowling front, leggie, Rabeya Khan, and right-arm pacer Marufa Akter have been the shining lights for the hosts. A collective bowling effort from the likes of Sultana Khatun, Nahida Akter, and Fariha Trisna will remain key to Bangladesh's success. Looking at this series as part of their preparations for the T20 World Cup scheduled to be played later in the year in Bangladesh, India has begun on a positive note. With the ball, Renuka Singh did the bulk of the damage in the first game, while it was the Indian spin trio of Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, and Radha Yadav who ruled the roost, picking 7 of the 10 wickets in the last outing. Promoted to number 3 in the last game, Dayalan Hemalatha did not disappoint, and she will be looking to carry the momentum forward. India's batting has not quite been put to the test yet, and it will be interesting to see how the likes of Smriti Mandhana, Yastika Bhatia, and Harmanpreet Kaur fare under pressure on what have so far been sluggish surfaces. Will India make it 3-0? Or will Bangladesh pull one back? We shall find out.
